name: Case study and reference development
oneliner: We turn work your teams already delivered into the proof material every future pursuit will lean on.
metaTitle: Case study and reference development | Techno War Room
metaDescription: We interview your delivery teams, verify the facts, and build case studies in the versions pursuits actually need: one-pager, proposal insert, deck slide, and reference brief.

scenarios.title: Buyers want proof
scenarios.text: The evaluation asks for three relevant references and you send three bullet points and a logo you are not sure you are allowed to use.

scenarios.title: Great work, no record
scenarios.text: Delivery did something genuinely impressive last year. Nobody wrote it down, and the people who remember it are on other projects now.

scenarios.title: Same story, worse every time
scenarios.text: Every proposal reconstructs the same case summary from memory, under deadline, in a slightly different and slightly weaker version.

what: We interview your delivery team, extract the story, and verify every fact with you before anything is written down as final. Then we build the case study in the versions a pursuit actually needs: the one-pager, the proposal insert, the deck slide, and the reference brief for calls.
Everything is filed in a library so the next pursuit starts with proof instead of a blank page.

deliverables.name: Case study one-pager
deliverables.desc: The standalone version for early conversations and attachments.

deliverables.name: Proposal insert
deliverables.desc: The version formatted to drop straight into an RFP response or proposal document.

deliverables.name: Deck slide version
deliverables.desc: The one-slide telling for presented pursuits, built to survive a committee.

deliverables.name: Reference brief
deliverables.desc: What your reference contact should expect to be asked, and the facts they can stand behind.

steps.title: Pick the wins
steps.text: We shortlist the delivered work with the most pursuit value: relevance, recency, and a story worth telling.

steps.title: Interview
steps.text: One structured interview per story with the people who delivered it, using our interview kit.
steps.need: An hour with each delivery lead

steps.title: Draft and verify
steps.text: We write the story. You verify every fact, figure, and name before it goes anywhere.

steps.title: Version and file
steps.text: Each verified story becomes its four pursuit-ready versions, filed in your library.

excludes: We do not invent numbers. If a result was not measured, the story is told without it.
We do not publish or name clients without your consent process being followed first.
We do not do brand design. The material lands in your templates, not a new visual identity.
We do not contact your clients. Reference conversations stay yours.

shape.v: Three to five stories at a time
Standing capture, one story after each major delivery

domains.name: B2B SaaS
domains.note: Outcome metrics carry SaaS stories. Where nothing was measured, adoption and timeline tell it instead.

domains.name: IT services
domains.note: Delivery stories sell: team shape, method, and what went wrong and got fixed read as credibility.

domains.name: BFSI
domains.note: Client names are often unusable. Anonymised stories need enough specificity to stay credible.

domains.name: Healthcare
domains.note: Consent and privacy rules shape what can be told. The reference brief does extra work here.
